blocks.html: A formula is an instruction to calculate. It always begins with =. When a value it uses changes, the result updates automatically.
Order of operations (BODMAS): brackets → ^ → * and / → + and - → & → comparisons. So =10+20/5 gives 14, while =(10+20)/5 gives 6.

rows: Changes with the new position: =B2*C2 in D2 becomes =B3*C3 in D3
Never changes — used for a fixed rate such as GST in one cell
Only the row or only the column changes

blocks.html: Write =B2*C2 once in D2 and drag the fill handle to D4: the relative references adjust for each row. If you needed every row to use the GST rate in C6, you would write $C$6 so that it does not shift.
A function is a built-in formula with a name and arguments in brackets:
=FUNCTION(argument1, argument2, …) . You can type it, use Insert Function (Shift + F3),
or use AutoSum (Alt + =).

rows: Counts cells that meet a condition
Adds cells that meet a condition
TRUE only if both are true

blocks.html: VLOOKUP finds a value in the first column of a table and returns a value from another column of the same row.
=VLOOKUP(lookup_value, table_range, column_number, FALSE)
Example: A price list has item codes in A2:A50, names in column B and prices in column C.
=VLOOKUP(105, A2:C50, 3, FALSE) returns the price of item 105. FALSE means exact
match.

blocks.html: Press Ctrl + ` (the grave accent key, left of 1) to show all formulas instead of results.

items.html: Sort (Data tab): arrange rows in ascending (A→Z, 0→9) or descending order. Custom Sort sorts by several columns, e.g. first by Section, then by Total (largest first). Always select the whole table so that each row stays together.

Filter (Ctrl + Shift + L): adds drop-down arrows to the headings. Show only certain rows, e.g. Section = B, or Total greater than 400. Hidden rows are not deleted. Click Clear Filter to show all again.

Chart area — the whole chart; plot area — where the data is drawn.
Chart title, axis titles, horizontal (category) axis, vertical (value) axis.
Legend — key to the colours of each series.
Data series and data labels — the bars, lines or slices and their values.
Gridlines — guide lines across the plot area.

blocks.html: Sparklines (Insert → Sparklines) are tiny charts inside a single cell, e.g. a small line showing each student's marks across five tests.
The Insert tab adds objects that float above the cells:

items.html: Pictures — from the computer or online (e.g. a school logo).
Shapes — arrows, boxes, callouts.
Icons and 3D models in newer versions.
SmartArt — ready-made diagrams for processes and hierarchies.
Text Box and WordArt — free-floating or decorative text.
Hyperlink (Ctrl + K) — a link to a website, another sheet or a file.
Header & Footer — text or a picture on every printed page.

blocks.html: The Picture Format tab lets you crop, resize, add borders, correct brightness and apply styles.
Did you know? Excel has more than 450 built-in functions, but most office work uses fewer than 20 of them. Master SUM, AVERAGE, COUNTIF, IF and VLOOKUP and you can handle most real-world tasks.
Aim: To use formulas, functions, sorting, filtering and charts on real data.

items.html: Formulas begin with = and follow BODMAS. Operators: arithmetic, comparison and & for joining text.
Relative references change when copied; absolute references ($A$1 ) stay fixed; F4 switches between them.
Functions include SUM, AVERAGE, MAX, MIN, COUNT, COUNTIF, SUMIF, ROUND, IF, AND, OR, text functions, date functions and VLOOKUP.
Error values such as #DIV/0! , #NAME? , #VALUE! , #REF! and #N/A point to specific mistakes.
Sorting arranges rows; filtering shows only matching rows.
Charts (column, bar, line, pie, area, scatter) present data visually; sparklines fit in one cell.
Pictures, shapes, SmartArt, text boxes and hyperlinks can be inserted from the Insert tab.
